name: CRITIC: LLMs Can Self-Correct with Tool-Interactive Critiquing
authors: Zhibin Gou, Zhihong Shao, Yeyun Gong, Yelong Shen, Yujiu Yang, Nan Duan, Weizhu Chen (Gou et al.); lead affiliations Tsinghua University and Microsoft Research Asia / Microsoft Azure AI
venue: ICLR 2024 (poster); arXiv first submitted 2023-05-19 as arXiv:2305.11738
reflection_type: tool-verified (verbal self-critique grounded by interaction with external tools: search engine, code interpreter, Perspective API)
feedback_source: external-tool (search engine for fact-checking, Python code interpreter for execution error messages/results, Perspective API toxicity scores); contrasted against pure self-generated feedback in the 'CRITIC w/o Tool' ablation
iteration_structure: iterative-refine (verify-then-correct loop, up to n=3 rounds for QA and n=4 for math program synthesis; stops early when output is unchanged for two consecutive corrections or critiques are satisfied)
reflection_object: output content — the model's initial answer/text/program is critiqued and progressively revised; for math it revises the generated program (block-level code) and for QA it revises the answer and underlying reasoning trace. No weights, prompts, or reusable skills are modified.
requires_training: none (training-free, plug-and-play on frozen black-box LLMs; uses only few-shot in-context demonstrations and text-to-text tool APIs)
reward_or_critic_model: none trained — the LLM acts as self-critic but its critique is grounded by external tool interaction (search results, interpreter execution feedback, Perspective API scores) which provides the reliable improvement signal
distillation_target: none (no reflection is distilled into a persistent artifact; corrections are applied in-context within the same task episode)
emergent_vs_engineered: prompt/scaffold-engineered — CRITIC uses ReAct-style few-shot in-context demonstrations to elicit the verify-then-correct behavior; the reflective behavior is engineered via prompting plus tool wiring, not RL-emergent
memory_type: short-term/scratchpad (the running context holds the initial output, tool-grounded critiques, and revised outputs within a task; a web-search caching mechanism stores API query results for reproducibility but is not agent memory)
memory_persistence: within-episode (corrections and critiques persist only across iterations of a single task instance; nothing carries across tasks or sessions)
memory_curation_mechanism: n/a (within-episode context only; no cross-episode memory store to curate; iteration stops via convergence/early-stopping rather than memory pruning)
error_localization_granularity: response-level for QA (revise the whole answer guided by retrieved evidence) and block-level (code) for mathematical program synthesis (interpreter error messages / execution results localize the faulty program); toxicity is attribute-level via Perspective API fine-grained scores
intra_task_vs_inter_task: intra-task (refine within a single task instance via iterative verify-then-correct; no transfer of experience across tasks)
failure_recovery_vs_avoidance: post-hoc-revision (generates an initial output, then critiques and revises it after the fact; the verify-then-correct loop is post-hoc per the paper's own Table 4 taxonomy)
task_domains: QA/reasoning (free-form / open-domain & multi-hop factual QA), math (mathematical program synthesis / arithmetic reasoning), general-alignment (toxicity reduction); tool-use throughout
benchmarks: AmbigNQ, TriviaQA, HotpotQA (free-form QA); GSM8k, SVAMP, TabMWP (mathematical program synthesis); RealToxicityPrompts (toxicity reduction, scored with Perspective API)
headline_result: On ChatGPT (gpt-3.5-turbo), CRITIC yields +7.7 average F1 across the three QA tasks, +7.0 absolute accuracy across the three math reasoning tasks, and a 79.2% relative reduction in toxicity probability — all without any additional data or training; e.g. on GSM8k CRITIC reaches 78.2 (+5.7 over PoT 72.5).
baselines: QA: Vanilla few-shot, CoT, Self-Consistency, ReAct, ReAct->CRITIC, CRITIC w/o Tool, Rejection Sampling, supervised SoTA. Math: Vanilla, Program-of-Thought (PoT), CRITIC w/o Tool, plus PAL and Self-Refine on Codex (from Madaan et al.). Toxicity: GPT-2, PPLM, GeDi, DEXPERTS, DAPT, PPO, Quark, Self-Correct (Welleck et al.), and base LLM. Across base LLMs: text-davinci-003, gpt-3.5-turbo (ChatGPT), and LLaMA-2 7B/13B/70B.
gains_vs_baseline: QA F1 over the model's own CoT initialization: +5.6 (text-davinci-003) and +7.7 (ChatGPT) for CRITIC; +10.3 and +12.4 in the CRITIC* oracle setting. CRITIC beats ReAct by avg +5.1 / +8.2 F1 on the two LLMs. Math GSM8k: +5.7 over PoT on ChatGPT (72.5 -> 78.2); TabMWP gains scale with model size: +4.7 / +9.4 / +16.0 on LLaMA-2 7B/13B/70B. Toxicity (ChatGPT): max toxicity 0.325 -> 0.173 and toxicity probability 0.192 -> 0.040. Critically, the 'CRITIC w/o Tool' ablation contributes marginally or harms QA (-0.03 / +2.33 F1) and causes a 1.8-point drop on text-davinci-003 math, showing tool feedback is the load-bearing component.
compute_cost_profile: Inference-time overhead grows linearly with the number of iterations n: e.g. two correction rounds for math program synthesis cost roughly 2x the single-pass PoT baseline (plus external tool/API calls per iteration). Authors note this is comparable to ReAct and far cheaper than Self-Consistency (which needs dozens to thousands of samples); benefits are largely realized within 1-3 iterations. No training/gradient cost (training-free).
known_limitations: (1) Relies on appropriate manually-crafted few-shot ReAct-style demonstrations; different prompt constructions affect results and consume long context. (2) Inference latency scales linearly with iteration count plus external tool calls. (3) Evaluated only on textual modality and a limited set of tasks; effectiveness on other tasks/LLMs uncertain because the model may not always be able to leverage suitable external feedback. (4) Depends on availability and reliability of external tools (search/interpreter/Perspective API); temporal inconsistency of the Google API threatens reproducibility (mitigated via caching). (5) Without reliable external feedback, self-correction yields only modest gains or degrades performance.
oracle_or_external_feedback_dependency: external-tool/verifier — the central thesis: improvement is consistent only with feedback from external tool interaction (search engine, code interpreter, Perspective API). The paper demonstrates that purely intrinsic self-verification/self-correction is unreliable. (Note: the CRITIC* variant additionally uses an oracle-label setting that corrects only known-incorrect samples to upper-bound performance.)
self_correction_efficacy: task-dependent / requires external verifier — net-positive and consistent WITH grounded tool feedback, but intrinsic self-correction (CRITIC w/o Tool) gives only marginal gains or net-negative results (e.g. -0.03 F1 on QA for text-davinci-003, -1.8/-3.3 points on some math, and worsened toxicity). The paper is an early empirical argument that self-correction does not work without reliable external feedback.
calibration_effect: mixed / not-formally-measured as calibration — the paper analyzes self-verification reliability via uncertainty estimation (intrinsic confidence and expressed uncertainty) and finds LLMs are unreliable self-verifiers, with intrinsic self-correction sometimes worsening performance; it does not report a formal calibration metric or 'reasoning tax' on reasoning-native models.
failure_attribution_capability: n/a (CRITIC is a self-correction method, not a failure-attribution/diagnosis system; it does not produce a failure-mode taxonomy or attribute responsible agents/steps in a multi-agent sense)
failure_mode_addressed: Targets hallucinated/untruthful facts and outdated knowledge (QA, via search), flawed/non-executable code and faulty reasoning traces (math, via interpreter), and offensive/toxic generation (via Perspective API). Centrally exposes the failure mode of superficial/unreliable self-reflection — i.e. LLMs cannot reliably self-verify or self-correct without external grounding.
dataset_or_benchmark_released: No new evaluation benchmark released; uses existing datasets (AmbigNQ, TriviaQA, HotpotQA, GSM8k, SVAMP, TabMWP, RealToxicityPrompts). Released code/prompts (microsoft/ProphetNet/CRITIC) and a reusable web-search tool (ZubinGou/llm-agent-web-tools) with cached API results for reproducibility.
builds_on: ReAct (Yao et al., 2023) — adopts its interleaved reasoning+tool prompting style; Program-of-Thought / PoT (Chen et al., 2022) and CoT (Wei et al., 2022) for initialization; tool-augmented LMs (Toolformer, PAL); contrasts with intrinsic self-correction works Self-Refine (Madaan et al., 2023), Reflexion (Shinn et al., 2023), Self-Critique (Saunders et al., 2022), CAI (Bai et al., 2022b), Self-Correct (Welleck et al., 2023), and RARR (Gao et al., 2022a).
extended_by_or_inspired: Cited alongside and contrasted with the broader self-correction literature; its core finding (external feedback is necessary for reliable self-correction) aligns with and is reinforced by analyses such as Huang et al. 2023 'Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet' and Stechly et al. 2023 'GPT-4 Doesn't Know It's Wrong'. It is a frequently-cited reference point for tool-grounded / verifier-grounded self-correction and tool-interactive agent frameworks. [Forward citation-graph walk not retrievable via API at query time; specific named successors marked uncertain.]
citation_count: Approximately 740 (Semantic Scholar, as of mid-2025; CorpusId 258823123)
reasoning_model_native: No — predates and does not target o1/R1-style reasoning models with built-in reflection; evaluated on text-davinci-003, gpt-3.5-turbo, and LLaMA-2. Its thesis (intrinsic self-correction is unreliable without external feedback) is, however, frequently invoked in debates about reasoning-model self-correction.
on_policy_distillation_link: None — CRITIC performs no distillation and no weight updates; it is purely in-context, training-free self-correction, so it is orthogonal to on-policy distillation / skill-optimization threads.
sample_efficiency: High in iterations: most benefit is obtained within 1-3 verify-then-correct rounds (QA uses up to n=3, math up to n=4 corrections), with diminishing marginal returns after 2-3 iterations; far more sample-efficient than Self-Consistency which needs 10-20+ samples for voting.
